question: How hard does the alignment + geo filter intersection cut random candidates at the truth-100%-retention threshold, and are the filters orthogonal?
hypothesis: The filter intersection rejects nearly all random candidates and the two filters test weakly-correlated physics.
narrative_md: Post-processing on s021: at per-seed truth-retention=100% threshold the filter intersection rejects 100% of random candidates on the median seed (99.1% cohort mean). Filters are weakly correlated (Pearson 0.167 / Spearman 0.189) so they test different physics and the intersection cuts harder than either alone. The cohort-tail (low-rot, zero-classifiable) is preserved by alignment alone.
